symbols.name: ambient space
symbols.meaning: The finite-dimensional vector space over $F$ on which every projection acts.
symbols.quote: Let $W$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over the field $F$.

symbols.name: subspace
symbols.meaning: A subspace of $W$ onto which a vector is projected.

symbols.name: complementary subspace
symbols.meaning: A subspace of $W$ meeting $U$ only in $0$ and with $U$ spanning $W$ together with it.
symbols.quote: A subspace $Y$ is complementary to $U$ when $U \cap Y = \{0\}$ and $U + Y = W$.

symbols.name: component in U
symbols.meaning: The part of a vector $x$ lying in $U$ in its split $x = x_U + x_Y$.
symbols.quote: Write $x = x_U + x_Y$, where $x_U$ is the component of $x$ in $U$ and $x_Y$ is its component in $Y$.

symbols.name: component in Y
symbols.meaning: The part of a vector $x$ lying in $Y$ in its split $x = x_U + x_Y$.
symbols.quote: Write $x = x_U + x_Y$, where $x_U$ is the component of $x$ in $U$ and $x_Y$ is its component in $Y$.

symbols.name: projection along Y
symbols.meaning: The map sending each vector $x$ to its component $x_U$ in $U$.
symbols.quote: The projection onto $U$ along $Y$ is the map $\Theta$ sending $x$ to $x_U$.

symbols.name: bilinear form
symbols.meaning: The nondegenerate bilinear form on $W$ whose orthogonality defines the complements $U^\perp$.
symbols.quote: Let $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ be a bilinear form on $W$, assumed nondegenerate: only $0$ is orthogonal to every vector of $W$.

symbols.name: orthogonal complement
symbols.meaning: The set of vectors orthogonal to every vector of $U$.
symbols.quote: Its orthogonal complement is $U^\perp = \{x : \langle u,x\rangle = 0 \text{ for all } u \in U\}$.

symbols.name: label projection
symbols.meaning: The projection onto $U$ along $U^\perp$, which the paper writes $P_U$.

symbols.name: larger nested subspace
symbols.meaning: A nondegenerate subspace containing $U$, the larger of two nested labels.

relations.quote: A projection along a subspace is built from [Linear algebra basics](linear-algebra-basics.md) alone.
